metadata.summary: The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) is a longitudinal multisite observational study launched in 2004 to develop clinical, imaging, and biomarker measures for the early detection and tracking of Alzheimer's disease (AD). It collects and shares MRI and PET imaging, cognitive/clinical assessments, CSF and blood biomarkers, and genomic data across approximately 2,300+ participants spanning cognitively normal aging, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's dementia.
metadata.purpose: To define biomarkers of disease progression to improve trial design and diagnostic accuracy.

modality.scope: Alzheimer's disease spectrum (cognitively normal, MCI, AD dementia)

ethics.license: Data Use Agreement (DUA) required; research use only, not open access.
ethics.privacy_measures: De-identification per HIPAA standards; centralized IRB oversight.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with US federal regulations (HIPAA, Common Rule), FDA guidance, and institutional IRB requirements.
ethics.bias_impact_assessment: Volunteer/survivor selection bias and limited ethnic diversity acknowledged as limitations affecting equity and generalizability.

known_limitations: Focuses only on the AD spectrum
Limited diversity in age/ethnicity beyond the enrolled cohort
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: US/Canada-centric enrollment; limited diversity in age/ethnicity; volunteer/survivor bias.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Underrepresentation of rare AD subtypes and non-White ethnic groups.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Results may not generalize to non-North American populations, younger/older age groups outside 55–90 range, or individuals with comorbidities excluded from enrollment.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Primarily covers White, non-Hispanic participants aged 55–90 in US/Canada; limited coverage of Hispanic, Black, Asian, Indigenous, and other racial/ethnic groups.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Missingness due to attrition, protocol non-adherence, and technical failures (e.g., incomplete scans, assay failures).

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Real-time clinical decision support; direct diagnostic use without regulatory validation.

data_origin.selection_rationale: To develop clinical, imaging, and biomarker measures for the early detection and tracking of Alzheimer's disease (AD).
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Longitudinal multisite observational cohort; participants selected to span cognitively normal aging, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's dementia.
data_origin.data_shifts_overtime: Follow-on phases (ADNI1, ADNI2, ADNI3) introduce changes in acquisition protocols, scanner models, and biomarker assays over time.

population.target_population: Individuals across the Alzheimer's disease spectrum: cognitively normal aging, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's dementia.
population.ethnicity_distribution: Limited diversity in age/ethnicity beyond the enrolled cohort.
population.inclusion_criteria: Cognitively normal, MCI, or AD diagnosis; age 55–90; specific clinical and imaging eligibility per phase.
population.exclusion_criteria: Major psychiatric illness, significant neurological disease other than AD, contraindications to MRI/PET.
population.missing_groups: Limited diversity in ethnicity and age beyond enrolled cohort; underrepresentation of non-US/non-Canadian populations.
population.subgroups_disparate_outcomes: US/Canada-centric enrollment may limit generalizability to global populations; volunteer/survivor selection bias may affect representation of advanced disease or frail elderly.

annotation.annotation_method: Clinical diagnosis by expert consensus; image annotations by trained raters using standardized protocols (e.g., Freesurfer, AV45 amyloid quantification).

annotators.qualifications: Trained raters and expert consensus panels

annotation.labeling_provenance: Clinical diagnosis and imaging biomarker labels derived from standardized protocols and expert review.
